MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Transform lives, every single day

Do you want a career that means more? At Anglicare Sydney, we bring the strength, the support and the strategy to make it happen. 

For over 170 years, Anglicare has supported people and communities across Sydney and the surrounds. We are looking for a Workplace AI Product Owner to own and manage the Workplace AI product within our Digital and AI Enablement team.

The Workplace AI Product Owner is responsible for the end-to-end ownership of Anglicare's workplace AI product ecosystem. Operating within Digital and AI Enablement group of products, this role has organisation-wide reach and manages a growing portfolio of workplace AI capabilities, adoption pathways, enablement assets, governance processes, and approved automation scenarios that improve productivity, decision support, and staff effectiveness.

As part of a purpose-driven organisation, you will be working in a people-centred, collaborative, and values-led environment where your work directly contributes to enriching lives and strengthening communities.

Your opportunity

The Workplace AI Product Owner will maximise organisational value from workplace AI, by owning the systems, experiences, and enablement approaches that help staff adopt endorsed AI capabilities safely, practically, and at scale, continuously improving how workplace AI supports productivity, decision quality, and operational effectiveness through shared governance, insight, and product-led delivery.

With ownership, you will manage the following:

Product Ownership and Delivery

Translate the Workplace AI strategy and roadmap into prioritised initiatives, use cases, and delivery activities, ensuring the highest-value opportunities are progressed first.

Manage the full lifecycle of roadmap items with continual review, optimisation, and scaling of Workplace AI capabilities, while retiring or reshaping low-value approaches where appropriate.

Collaborate with delivery, architecture, and engineering teams to shape solutions that are valuable, usable, feasible, and scalable within the broader digital ecosystem.

Maintain an understanding of organisational priorities, workforce needs, AI market developments, and internal constraints to ensure the product evolves in line with strategic direction.

Adoption and Enablement

Design and deliver role-based adoption and enablement approaches, including training pathways, communities of practice, champions, practical playbooks, and targeted support materials.

Lead internal communications and engagement for Workplace AI, sharing practical guidance, success stories, updates, and use case examples that build awareness and confidence.

Establish fair and transparent prioritisation for rollout, licensing, and training so adoption is value-led, scalable, and equitable across teams

Identify user needs and pain points, using feedback and insight to continuously improve the workplace AI experience and increase sustained adoption.

Governance and Platform Enablement

Partner with business, technology, cyber, privacy teams to ensure Workplace AI use cases are safe, responsible, and aligned to enterprise governance requirements.

Enable approved automation and agent scenarios that extend Workplace AI outcomes, while working within enterprise guardrails and partnering with business owners for implementation and operational support.

Coordinate remediation plans for identified Workplace AI risks and findings with cyber and relevant 3rd party owners and support governance forums with clear reporting and decision material.

Build strong relationships across leadership, business, and technology teams to align stakeholders around priorities, investment choices, and responsible adoption.

Benefits Realisation and Insights

Define, measure, and report on Workplace AI product KPIs, adoption indicators, and benefit outcomes across personas and use cases.

Quantify how Workplace AI initiatives contribute to business outcomes such as time savings, improved quality, reduced cycle time, stronger decision support, and workforce effectiveness.

Use data, feedback, and experimentation to validate opportunities, inform prioritisation, and guide future investment decisions.

What you'll bring:

You will be equipped with the following skills.

Gen AI, automation or digital transformation initiatives

Product management (Agile, discovery-delivery)

Change management

Stakeholder engagement and communication

Technical fluency and systems thinking

Benefits realisation and performance measurement

You will also need:

Bachelor's degree in digital, technology, business, or a related field.

5+ years experience in product management, digital workplace, or a related role; or 1-2 years experience in gen AI enablement

Experience leading adoption, change, enablement, or capability uplift initiatives across diverse user groups.

Hands-on experience with Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, Power Automate, Anthropic Claude

Why Anglicare?

At Anglicare, we provide meaningful opportunities and choice - both for the communities we support and the people who work with us. 

Here's what you'll enjoy: 

Flexible work options to balance life and career. 

Salary packaging benefits - up to $15,900 of your income tax free, plus $2,650 for meals and entertainment. 

Ongoing professional development and career pathways. 

Exclusive staff discounts with over 400 retailers. 

Employee Assistance Program and Fitness Passport with access to 800+ gyms. 

Belonging to a supportive, purpose-driven team committed to making a difference. 

Apply now

Are you ready to help us attract and empower the people who will shape Anglicare's future? To apply, click the 'Apply' button and submit your resum and cover letter. All applicants will receive a response. Anglicare is as wonderfully diverse as the communities we serve. While guided by our Christian values, our team includes people of all faiths and backgrounds.

We strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, and people of all ages, genders, abilities and cultural backgrounds.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.









Shape Digital Healthcare. Drive Innovation. Improve Lives. 












About the Department of Clinical Informatics 






The Department of Clinical Informatics is where healthcare and technology come together to transform patient care. 






Established in 2025, we bring together clinical, digital and innovation expertise to shape the future of healthcare across Monash Health. Our multidisciplinary team spans Nursing, Medical, Allied Health and Community Informatics, Digital Clinical Learning and Change, Artificial Intelligence, Consumer Informatics, User Experience and Clinical Coding. 






The Department is committed to building a high-performing team and improving patient outcomes through digital innovation, aligned with the Monash Health Strategic Plan and Digital & Data Plan. 






If you're passionate about innovation, collaboration and using technology to make a real difference in healthcare, this newly created full-time, ongoing role offers the chance to help shape the future from the ground up. 












About the Role 






This ground-breaking role is designed to enable our clinical teams to readily and safely transform patient care, using digital technologies. Intersecting with clinical practice, digital health, change management and workplace capability building, this is a rare opportunity to lead the transition of our clinicians, in all professional streams, to embrace the benefits of a digitally thinking workplace. 






Far from a "Business As Usual" role, this opportunity will suit individuals seeking to leverage strategic leadership and advice to engineer a significant change in the way we deliver patient care. Acknowledging the rapid rate of change in the digital space, you are not deterred by uncertainty. If appointed, you will relish the chance to apply your innovative thinking skills to build diverse, agile, high performing teams. 






As a key member of our Clinical Informatics leadership team, your success will be measured across three key result areas: 









Leadership of change of learning functions and practices 












Collaboration with Clinical Informatics and Digital and Information Division 












Stakeholder engagement and relationship development 









You'll appreciate that the collaborative nature of this role will see you working on site at least three days per week, with flexible working arrangements available. With accountability for the function across the whole of organisation, travel across Monash Health will be required. 












About You 






You have a keen understanding of informatics as well as demonstrated knowledge of adult learning principles. Described as visionary, you also have the ability to translate organisational objectives into practical and effective practices that advance care at the operational level. 






You are comfortable working with ambiguity. Your emotional intelligence equips you with the skills and strategies to navigate the challenges of change respectfully, professionally and sensitively, adapting your style to meet the needs of varying audiences. 






Our clinical teams are highly skilled, busy and saturated with information. Your job will be to enhance their Joy in Work through equipping them with a relevant, digitally-enabled approach that will see them continue to deliver consistently high standards of care in the community we serve. 



What you need 






Your ability to engage and influence effectively across a range of professional groups, pivoting seamlessly between clinical, technical and strategic perspectives, will be key to your success. 






To be considered for this role, you'll need to demonstrate: 









Deep clinical systems expertise and success leading enterprise change 












Strategic leadership of integrated change and learning functions to drive enterprise-wid digitatl transformation 












Intimate appreciation of transformation as it relates to building digital capability 












Expertise in adult learning, enabling success driving digital adoption and optimisation 












Awareness of digital architecture and how systems communicate, share, exchange and use data 












Detailed knowledge of clinical safety and risk management 












Data and information fluency 









Current Ahpra registration, a postgraduate qualification in Digital Health, Informatics, Learning-Education, Change Management and-or leadership are required. 












Why join Monash Health? 






This is more than a digital role-it's your chance to transform healthcare at scale. Working at the intersection of clinical care, technology and innovation, you'll help create smarter digital solutions that improve patient outcomes and support the clinicians who deliver them every day 












At Monash Health, you will: 









Lead a state-wide service with real impact 












Work within a values-driven, purpose-led organisation 












Be part of a connected network of clinical, academic and system leaders 












Help drive innovation, inclusion and better health outcomes 















We offer: 









The opportunity to make a real impact on patient experience 












A supportive, collaborative team environment 












Ongoing learning and development opportunities 












The chance to be part of Victoria's largest public health service

 Embedded directly within the high-volume  Linen Services Department , this position offers an immediate start with a clear  temp-to-perm pathway . Prove your diagnostic and plant maintenance skills on-site and transition into a permanent, secure public sector career. 
  The Package & Perks  
 
 
  Competitive Hourly Rate:   $56.95 per hour + Super  (paid weekly). 
 
 
  Flexible Roster:  Choose your own start and finish times, provided your standard daily hours are worked within a flexible  6:00 AM to 6:00 PM  window.

  Career Security:  Strong temp-to-perm pathway to secure a permanent footprint within public sector infrastructure.

 Working within a heavy industrial processing environment on a hospital campus, you will focus on the mechanical upkeep, overhauls, and breakdown response for high-capacity industrial plant equipment.

Our client is a rapidly growing, premier original equipment manufacturer (OEM) specialising in high-end industrial fluid systems, dewatering packages, and heavy-duty custom skid builds for the Australian mining and resources sectors.

  The Mindset:  Absolute attention to detail is paramount. You must be someone who takes genuine pride in the neatness, routing, and precision of your mechanical builds. 
 
 
  Technical Strengths:  Strong experience dealing with rotating equipment, hydraulic hoses, pipework, and instrument integration.
